title: China’s Long Twilight
gist: Teaser of Carl Minzner's essay arguing China faces a long twilight of demographic decline and political paralysis. China's working-age share rose from 57 percent in 1978 to nearly 75 percent in 2010, powering 20-fold growth, but the one-child policy and East Asian low-fertility forces have produced three decades of below-replacement births, turning that tide over the past decade.

insights.claim: China's working-age population (ages 15 to 64) rose from 57 percent of the population in 1978 to a peak of nearly 75 percent in 2010.
insights.so_what: The labor-force tailwind behind China's growth has peaked and is reversing.
insights.quote: The working-age population (those aged 15 to 64) rose from 57 percent of the population in 1978 to a peak of nearly 75 percent in 2010.
insights.locator: During the boom years of the reform era
insights.speaker: Carl Minzner

insights.claim: China's expanding workforce powered three decades of close to ten percent annual growth, a 20-fold economic expansion, during the reform era from 1978 to the early 2000s.
insights.so_what: Growth that was demographically driven is unlikely to be replicated as the workforce shrinks.
insights.quote: three decades of close to ten percent annual growth—a 20-fold economic expansion.
insights.locator: During the boom years of the reform era
insights.speaker: Carl Minzner

insights.claim: Beijing's one-child policy and the social forces that pushed East Asian fertility to historic lows have produced three decades of below-replacement birth rates, turning China's demographic tide over the past decade.
insights.so_what: Structural headwind for Chinese growth, property demand and fiscal sustainability.
insights.quote: But over the past decade, this tide has turned.
insights.speaker: Carl Minzner

insights.claim: Carl Minzner argues China is entering a long twilight in which demographic decline combines with political paralysis, with implications for the fate of great powers.
insights.so_what: Supports a structurally lower long-run growth and power trajectory for China.
insights.speaker: Carl Minzner
